item.description: The SubprocessCLITransport.receive_messages() method is not properly implemented as an async iterator. Tests are failing with "TypeError: 'async for' requires an object with __aiter__ method, got coroutine" because the method doesn't correctly implement the async iterator protocol.
item.contract: The receive_messages() method must return a proper AsyncIterator[dict[str, Any]] that can be used with async for loops. It should yield parsed message dictionaries asynchronously and properly implement the async iteration protocol.

item.description: The SubprocessCLITransport.send_request() method has incorrect handling of AsyncIterable inputs, causing issues with session ID handling in test test_send_message_with_session_id.
item.contract: The send_request() method should properly handle AsyncIterable inputs and correctly pass session IDs to messages when sending them to the CLI subprocess.

item.description: The SubprocessCLITransport.interrupt() method is not properly implemented - the test test_interrupt is failing with assert False, indicating the interrupt mechanism isn't working correctly.
item.contract: The interrupt() method should correctly send a control request to the subprocess and wait for confirmation, allowing the client to properly handle interruptions during streaming.

item.description: The SubprocessCLITransport._stream_to_stdin() method is not properly handling AsyncIterable prompts, causing connection issues and preventing proper message streaming.
item.contract: The _stream_to_stdin() method should properly handle AsyncIterable prompts by iterating over them and sending each message to stdin in the correct format with proper session IDs.
item.acceptance: All streaming-related tests that depend on proper AsyncIterable handling

item.description: The ClaudeSDKClient.query() method has incorrect handling for AsyncIterable prompts, particularly around the transport replacement logic that breaks async iteration contracts.
item.contract: The query() method should properly handle AsyncIterable prompts by either reusing the existing transport connection or properly managing the transport lifecycle without breaking the async iteration contract.
item.acceptance: All tests involving query() with AsyncIterable prompts
